title: How Much Wood
subtitle: Approximant W
description: This exercise focuses on the /w/ sound, which requires lip rounding and a smooth glide into the following vowel. Repeating W-heavy phrases builds consistent muscle memory for this often-underarticulated sound.
tip: Round your lips into a tight circle before voicing each /w/ — think of it as the shape you make to blow out a candle, then glide smoothly into the vowel.
phrases: How much wood would a woodchuck chuck if a woodchuck could chuck wood?
A woodchuck would chuck all the wood he could chuck if a woodchuck could chuck wood.
How many boards could the Mongols hoard if the Mongol hordes got bored?
Whether the weather is warm, whether the weather is hot, we have to put up with the weather, whether we like it or not.
Which witch wished which wicked wish?
Will you always allow a wall-eyed walrus to wander in the wildwood?
